question: When should a provision be recognised under Ind AS 37? How does a provision differ from a contingent liability?

points.label: Present obligation
points.description: There is a present obligation (legal or constructive) as a result of a past event.

points.label: Probable outflow
points.description: It is probable that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required.

points.label: Reliable estimate
points.description: A reliable estimate of the amount of the obligation can be made.

points.label: Contingent liability
points.description: A possible obligation whose existence depends on uncertain future events, or a present obligation where the outflow is not probable or cannot be measured reliably.

points.label: Different treatment
points.description: Provisions are recognised in the balance sheet; contingent liabilities are not recognised but disclosed, unless the outflow is remote.
